This decision has had a ripple effect unto this very day, and I would never have met my wife if it hadn't been for that decision.

I think that they have great underlying effects. Many of the thoughts I now think are based in books. I have gained major insights into other human beings because I read so much. I grew up in a fairly Islamophobic place in a fairly Islamophobic time. I remember thinking The Amazing Atheist and an older British gentlemen, whose Youtube handle I forgot, were so intelligent for their anti-religious views. However, I grew up reading books like The Breadwinner, The Kite Runner, A Thousand Splendid Suns, The Color of Water and more. I remember disagreeing with anger based people, like those I listed, because people in the Middle East and Muslims in general are just as flawed and noble as the rest of humanity. I also never met a black person until I was 16, but I understood the same thing, along with Jews, Africans, and so many different people. I never had to meet a Muslim to understand that the two of us might be similar or different, but we are not oppositional beings. I can think of a book that teach most of my major life philosophies. Likewise, I can also think of books that I thought were brilliant at the time, for example Ishmael, but later understood that books too can be flawed. That just because people in other countries, or in the case presented in Ishmael the continuant of Africa, are not 'productive' doesn't mean we should abandon them or think of them as below us. Ishmael tried to get me to abandom others, but A Long Way Gone taught me to never accept that some people are able to be discarded.

No single idea is perfect and for all important ideas a single sentence that describes it is inadequate. All different types of people are different typed of flawed, any example I listed. Getting older doesn't have to mean giving up on the ideas of youth, Le Petite Prince. It is okay to feel alone and lost, Catcher in the Rye. So, so, many life lessons learned from books. For each I could go on for a paragraph as long as my first, if not longer.
